question: Which events were initially announced as demonstration sports but later became full-fledged medal events in the 38th National Games held at Uttarakhand?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yogasana and Mallakhamb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yogasana** and **Mallakhamb** were initially introduced as demonstration sports in the 38th National Games held in Uttarakhand but were later upgraded to full-fledged medal events.
 
• **Yogasana** is a traditional Indian discipline involving physical postures (asanas) combined with breathing techniques (pranayama) and meditation. It has gained global recognition for promoting physical and mental well-being.
 
• **Mallakhamb** is an indigenous sport that involves acrobatics and yoga-like postures performed on a vertical wooden pole or rope. It is widely regarded as an ancient form of physical training in India.
 
• The decision to include these sports as medal events highlights India’s commitment to promoting traditional and indigenous sports on a national platform.
 
• The inclusion of Yogasana and Mallakhamb also aligns with the government’s efforts to preserve and promote India’s cultural heritage while encouraging physical fitness and mental discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kho-Kho and Kabaddi**

 
 
• Both are traditional Indian team sports that are immensely popular across the country.
 
• Kabaddi is a contact sport where players take turns raiding the opponent’s court to tag or tackle players while holding their breath.
 
• Kho-Kho is a tag-based game where speed, agility, and strategy play a key role. It involves chasing and touching opposing players in a predefined sequence.
 
• These sports have been long-standing medal events in national games and are not new additions or demonstration sports.
 
 
 
• **Shooting and Athletics**
 
 
• Both shooting and athletics are globally recognized sports and have been integral parts of the National Games in India for decades.
 
• Shooting involves precision-based events like rifle, pistol, and shotgun disciplines.
 
• Athletics includes a variety of track and field events such as running, jumping, and throwing, and is considered the backbone of any multi-sport event.
 
• These sports are not related to the context of being demonstration sports in the 38th National Games.
 
 
 
• **Kayaking and Rowing**
 
 
• These are water sports that involve paddling or rowing a boat through a water body.
 
• Kayaking uses a double-bladed paddle, while rowing requires participants to use oars in synchronization.
 
• Both sports are part of the National Games but were not introduced as demonstration sports in the 38th edition.
 
 
 
• **Significance of National Games**
 
 
• The National Games serve as a platform to promote sports culture and identify talent at the grassroots level in India.
 
• They aim to provide exposure to athletes and encourage participation in diverse sporting disciplines, including traditional and modern sports.
 
• The inclusion of indigenous sports like Yogasana and Mallakhamb reflects the government’s emphasis on promoting India’s rich sporting heritage.
